::: {.lead}
Today one job goes through three apps, as in Lectures 6, 7, 11 and 15.
There are no new ideas. **Part A** is in Excel, Word, PowerPoint and an AI
assistant on the lab computer; **Part B** is on a simulator of the
interactive page: on paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its
link. After each step, write your result in its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Excel, Word and PowerPoint (the desktop
  apps: Slides from Outline is in the desktop app of PowerPoint) and an AI
  assistant that the university allows (for example
  `copilot.microsoft.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Office.
- **The story:** Huda's summary of March is Paper 206 JD, Drinks 71 JD and
  Bags 78 JD. She needs the table, its total and a chart in her Word
  report, and three slides for the Monday meeting.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · From Excel to Word

**The idea (Lectures 6, 7 and 11):** Excel makes the numbers: a SUM
formula and a chart with a real title. Word gives the report its headings
(**Heading 1**). When you paste a table into Word, **Use Destination
Styles** gives a Word table in the look of the report that you can still
edit; **Picture** gives an image that nobody can change. A pasted table
does not follow Excel.

**Aim:** move a table and a chart from Excel into a Word report, in the
look of the report.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Excel and Word)**
:::

1. In Excel, type the summary table: *Type* and *Total (JD)*, then Paper
   206, Drinks 71 and Bags 78. In **B5**, type `=SUM(B2:B4)`. Select
   **A1:B4** and make a column chart with a real title.

   {{< record "B5 shows … ; my chart title …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **355 JD** (206 + 71 + 78): the total comes from the formula, not from
   typing. A real title, for example "Sales by type in March (JD)", never
   "Chart Title".
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="355" unit="JD" hint="206 + 71 + 78."}
   What does `=SUM(B2:B4)` show?

   Why: 206 + 71 + 78 = 355 JD. The total comes from the SUM formula, not from typing.
   :::

2. Make a new Word document and save it as `report.docx`. Type the heading
   *Sales by type* with the style **Heading 1**. Copy **A1:B5** in Excel
   and paste it under the heading with **Paste Options › Use Destination
   Styles**. Then copy the chart and paste it under the table.

   {{< record "The paste option … ; the table looks …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Use Destination Styles**: the table takes the font and the colours of
   the report, and it stays a table that you can edit. The chart comes
   under it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Why paste the table with **Use Destination Styles**?

   - [x] The table gets the look of the report, and you can still edit it.

     Why: Destination means the Word report: its styles give the look.

   - [ ] It pastes the table as a picture.

     Why: A picture cannot be edited: that is the option Picture.

   - [ ] It keeps the colours of Excel.

     Why: That is Keep Source Formatting.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-14/sims/office-relay.html" poster="../../week-14/sims/office-relay.png" title="Office Relay: six jobs in three apps" kind="game" >}}

3. Play **Office Relay**: six jobs in three apps. What is the right way for
   the job "The manager must read the report but must not change it"?

   {{< record "The manager's report: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Save a PDF copy and send it**: a PDF keeps the look, and people do not
   easily change it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Bags change from 78 to 98 JD in Excel. Does the table in the Word report
   change by itself?

   - [x] No: paste it again, or change it in Word.

     Why: A normal paste is a copy; it does not follow Excel.

   - [ ] Yes, at once.

     Why: The pasted table is a copy of the numbers.

   - [ ] Yes, when you save the report.

     Why: Saving does not bring the new numbers.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · From the report to slides, with AI help

**The idea (Lectures 7, 15 and 19):** PowerPoint can make slides from the
headings of a Word report (**Home › New Slide › Slides from Outline**): a
**Heading 1** line becomes a slide title, a **Heading 2** line becomes a
bullet, and Normal text, tables and charts stay out. Check every AI number
with the data before it goes on a slide.

**Aim:** make three slides from the report, with one checked AI sentence.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Word, PowerPoint and an AI assistant)**
:::

1. In `report.docx`, type *Total: 355 JD* right under the heading *Sales
   by type*, with the style **Heading 2**. At the end, type *The best
   week* (**Heading 1**), *Third week: 112 JD* (**Heading 2**) and *Thank
   you!* (**Heading 1**). Save and close the file. In a new presentation,
   choose **Home › New Slide › Slides from Outline** › `report.docx`.
   Delete the empty first slide, and save it as `talk.pptx`.

   {{< record "Slides … ; their titles …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **3 slides**: *Sales by type* (with the point *Total: 355 JD*), *The
   best week* (with *Third week: 112 JD*) and *Thank you!*. One slide for
   each Heading 1; the table and the chart stay out.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="3" unit="slides" hint="Count the lines with Heading 1."}
   How many slides does **Slides from Outline** make from the report?

   Why: One slide for each Heading 1 line: Sales by type, The best week and Thank you!
   :::

2. Ask the AI assistant: *Write one sentence about these March sales:* and
   paste only the table. Check its numbers with Excel. Put the true
   sentence in the notes of slide 1; correct a wrong number first.

   {{< record "The AI sentence … ; right or corrected …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Each number must match the table: 206, 71, 78 and 355 JD. A true
   sentence: "In March we sold for 355 JD, and Paper sold the most, 206
   JD."
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which AI sentence is true?

   - [x] In March we sold for 355 JD, and Paper sold the most, 206 JD.

     Why: Both numbers match the table in Excel.

   - [ ] In March we sold for 355 JD, and Bags sold the most.

     Why: Bags sold 78 JD; Paper sold the most, 206 JD.

   - [ ] In March we sold for 400 JD.

     Why: The SUM in Excel is 355 JD.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-14/sims/heading-slides.html" poster="../../week-14/sims/heading-slides.png" title="Heading Slides: Word headings to slides" >}}

3. In **Heading Slides**, do Task 1 and Task 2: give each line of the
   report the right style. Which style does the thanks get in Task 2, and
   how many slides are there?

   {{< record "The thanks: … ; slides: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Heading 1**: the thanks becomes the title of a third slide, so there
   are **3 slides**. In Task 1 the thanks is Normal, so it stays out.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which style does each line of the report get? Sort them.

   Heading 1: a slide title
   :   March sales

       Why: The title of slide 1.

   :   The best week

       Why: The title of slide 2.

   Heading 2: a bullet
   :   Total: 355 JD

       Why: A point of slide 1.

   :   Third week: 112 JD

       Why: A point of slide 2.
   :::
